rules.title: FDA Quality Management System Regulation (21 CFR Part 820)
rules.summary: Replaced the older Quality System Regulation and incorporated ISO 13485:2016 by reference, including its purchasing and supplier-control clause (7.4).
rules.why_it_matters: Safety-critical parts need suppliers you have evaluated and can show records for. A supplier without a quality certificate on file is exposed.
rules.workaround: Qualify and audit the supplier, or move volume to a supplier that already holds a certificate.

rules.title: FD&C Act s524B: cybersecurity for 'cyber devices'
rules.summary: Premarket submissions for connected devices must include a cybersecurity plan, a software bill of materials (SBOM) and a vulnerability-management plan.
rules.why_it_matters: Wireless modules and control boards bring third-party software into the device, so the supplier must supply SBOM data. This is documentation, not a ban.
rules.source: FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance and s524B
rules.workaround: Ask each wireless-module supplier for SBOM and patch-support commitments in the contract.

rules.title: EU MDR transition deadlines (Regulation 2023/607)
rules.summary: Extended legacy-device deadlines: until 31 Dec 2027 or 31 Dec 2028 depending on risk class, if conditions are met.
rules.why_it_matters: If you sell in the EU, supplier files and component traceability must meet MDR expectations before your class deadline.
rules.workaround: Check your device class; schedule supplier file reviews ahead of the deadline.

rules.title: EU proposal to simplify the MDR and IVDR
rules.summary: A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 1023) to reduce the burden of MDR and IVDR rules. It could change requirements and timelines.
rules.why_it_matters: Watch only: it is a proposal, so no exposure is calculated.
rules.workaround: Track passage before changing EU compliance plans.

rules.title: Section 232 investigation: PPE, medical consumables and medical equipment
rules.date_label: Opened 2 Sep 2025; no decision published as of Oct 2026
rules.summary: National-security investigation into imported medical devices, consumables and PPE. One source dated 28 Oct 2026 reports no report or proclamation has been published and the report deadline has passed.
rules.why_it_matters: A decision could land with little warning. If tariffs came, spend with non-U.S. suppliers would rise. Scope of component coverage is unknown, so the slider is a hypothetical.
rules.source: SPS Commerce, 'Section 232 Medical Device Tariffs: The Investigation That Never Closed' (28 Oct 2026)
rules.workaround: Dual-source key parts now, and price the U.S.-made alternative so you can switch quickly.
